previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with a complex history of fibrosing mesenteritis, recurrent small bowel obstructions, and G-tube dependence, was admitted for worsening abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. Imaging showed no acute obstruction but revealed adhesions causing dilation of the duodenum and proximal jejunum. She was managed conservatively with NPO status, G-tube suction, and IV pain control. TPN was initiated due to chronic malnutrition and continued at home. She developed a port-a-cath-associated coagulase-negative staph bacteremia, treated with two weeks of IV vancomycin and lock therapy, with negative follow-up cultures. Her G-tube was replaced twice during the stay due to leakage and accidental dislodgement. Due to subtherapeutic INR unresponsive to warfarin escalation, she was transitioned to enoxaparin for anticoagulation. She was discharged home with TPN, home health services, and plans for outpatient follow-up, including surveillance blood cultures.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo F with h/o fibrosing mesenteritis and multiple MRSA 
infections of POC admitted with fever and CONS bacteremia now 
with severe abdominal pain.

# Abdominal Pain/Nausea: Acute onset occurred on HD4. Sharp and 
severe in nature, non-radiating in LUQ and at times occured in 
RUQ. Quality different than prior SBOs. Two CT scans and 
enteroscopy performed could not illicit any source of patient's 
pain. Felt to be functional in nature. Persisted throughout 
hospitalization requiring narcotics. Interestingly, patient 
maintained on low dose dilaudid PCA and when transitioned to 
oral morphine of much higher potency, the patient had worsening 
pain suggesting a possibility of a psychiatric component to her 
pain as when she had control with a PCA, her pain improved. 
Eventually able to wean down to oral morphine... Received SC 
methyl naltrexone as has helped patient's pain in the past, 
however three doses given with minimal effect. She completed a 
seven day course of cipro/flagyl for empiric coverage for 
possible infectious etiology, however did not improve her pain. 
Palliative care and pain service consulted with limitations on 
what to give as patient has multiple allergies. She was 
ultimately discharged on neurontin, oral morphine, 
amitriptylline, a lidocaine patch and ativan. Regarding her 
nausea, initially on IV ativan and phenergan as patient has 
allergies to all other anti-emetics. Zyprexa tried with minimal 
effect. Eventually weaned down to po forms of ativan and 
phenergan with IV zofran for breakthrough and alternative 
treatments like acupuncture, meditation and ginger lozenges with 
improvement in patient's symptoms.Called ___ in 
___: ___ to confirm that they had enough MS 
oral solution for her prior to d/c. She will get further Rx's 
from ___ and further medication regimen titration via 
pain clinic. 

# CONS bacteremia: Source likely PICC as this culture was 
positive for CONS. Her PICC and Port a cath were removed on HD2 
given this was a recurrence from prior hospitalization after

showing sensitivity to vancomycin. Given a four week course with

# Fibrosing mesenteritis: Admitted for SBOs secondary to this in 
___ requiring a two month long admission and was medically 
treated. Followed by ___ in the outpatient clinic. 
Patient has had multiple surgeries and is no longer considered a 
surgical candidate per Dr. ___. Has G tube in place that 
did leak during admission and was replaced by ___ without 
incident. She was continued on TPN throughout hospitalization 
and GT was placed to gravity. Her G tube output increased when 
her po intake increased to the point that everything she took in 
orally came out through th GT. Octreotide was increased to 100 
mcg q8H. She was tried on a soft solid diet, but gave her 
significant abdominal pain. She was placed on a full liquid diet 
and given IVFs to match her losses. She will need to be on a 
full liquid diet at home with TPN to supplement and IVF to 
prevent dehydration as it seems she is incapable to absorb 
nutrients through her GI tract currently. to ensure her g tube 
output does not increase and disrupt her fluid balance. Dr. 
___ will continue to follow the patient to titrate her 
IVFs and consider alternative treatment options (although these 
are quite slim at this point).

# Depression: Severe at times with patient having passive and at 
times active suicidal ideations. Outpatient therapist highly 
concerned for patient's safety and she as well as medical team

code status to DNR, who refused. She was evaluated by psychiatry 
who felt her pain disorder was the primary problem with 
psychological manifestations and felt she was not a candidate 
for inpatient psychiatric admission. 

# Acute Renal Failure: Cr peaked at 1.2 from 0.8 in setting of 
bacteremia and increasing G tube outpute. Resolved with

the hub and removed over ___ wire.  A new 12 ___
catheter was placed over the guidewire and advanced to the stomach.  The
guidewire was removed and retaining pigtail formed and locked.  Contrast
injection through the newly placed catheter confirmed satisfactory position
and placement.  Catheter was flushed and capped.  Catheter secured to the skin
with 0 silk suture and a Flexi-Trak device.  Sterile dressings were applied. 
The patient tolerated the procedure well and there were no immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Partially pulled-out existing G-tube with leakage through the sideholes.
2.  Successful replacement of the G-tube with a new 12 ___
catheter.  The catheter is ready for use.

If leakage persists after this procedure, catheter upsizing to a 14 ___ MIC
G-tube needs to be considered; otherwise a routine catheter exchange will be
arranged in three months time.

INDICATION:  ___ female with history of fibrosing mesenteritis,
presents with bacteremia and sudden onset severe upper abdominal pain of
uncertain etiology.  Assess for acute process.

COMPARISON:  Multiple studies including most recent CT abdomen, ___ and upper GI small bowel follow-through, ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT-acquired axial images were obtained through the abdomen and
pelvis without IV contrast.  Oral contrast was administered.  Coronal and
sagittal reformats were displayed.

CT ABDOMEN WITHOUT IV CONTRAST:  There is dependent subsegmental atelectasis
at the lung bases.  Visualized portion of the heart and pericardium are
unremarkable.

The liver, pancreas and spleen are normal.  The gallbladder is surgically
absent.  The left adrenal gland is normal.  There is nodularity at the medial
limb of the right adrenal gland, likely an adenoma and unchanged from prior. 
The kidneys are symmetric in size with hypodensities which are too small to
further characterize, but likely simple cyst.  There is no evidence of
hydronephrosis or hydroureter.

The patient is status post multiple duodenal and small bowel surgeries. A PEG
tube is noted within the stomach extending.  The gastric folds are mildly
thickened.  The duodenum is redundant with calcification of the suture lines. 
There is marked dilatation of the duodenum, but the wall is thin where the
bowel is distended.  The jejunum is also distended with new wall thickening
and perijejunal fluid just beyond the ligament of Treitz. More distally, the
jejunum gently narrows, makes a tight bend with narrowing and feeds into a
conglomerate of bowel loops that appears tethered to the anterior abdominal
wall. Oral contrast does pass beyond the narrowing (2:53), but a partial
mechanical obstruction is possible particularly given the similiar appearance
on prior CT and small bowel follow through.  

There is no free air in the abdomen.  No mesenteric or retroperitoneal
lymphadenopathy meeting criteria for pathologic enlargement is noted.

CT PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST:  The urinary bladder, distal ureters, adnexa,
sigmoid colon and rectum are normal.  There is no free fluid in the pelvis. 
No pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy is present.

BONE WINDOWS:  No suspicious lytic or sclerotic osseous lesion is identified.
A metallic implant device is noted posterior to the T6 through T8 vertebral
bodies.

IMPRESSION: Similar dilated appearance of the duodenum and proximal jejunum
with new moderate wall thickening and perijejunal fluid beyond the ligament of
Treitz. As before, there is narrowing of the jejunum in the right mid abdomen,
which likely represents at least a partial mechanical obstruction related to
adhesions and is similar to the small bowel follow-through. Dilated proximal
bowel suggests severe chronic functional abnormality that correlates to prior
studies.

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  ___ female with severe abdominal pain, evaluate
for acute process.

___.

TECHNIQUE:  Following premedication for the prevention of contrast allergy,
oral and intravenous contrast was administered.  Approximately 120 cc of
iodinated intravenous contrast was hand injected through the patient's PICC.
Axial images were acquired of the abdomen and pelvis following this, and these
were reformatted into coronal and sagittal planes.

FINDINGS:

LUNG BASES:  There is bibasilar atelectasis without pleural or pericardial
effusion.  Note is made of calcifications of the coronary arteries.

ABDOMEN:  There is pneumobilia.  The liver is otherwise normal in appearance,
without focal lesions. Incidental note is made of a hepatic cyst (2; 31). The
portal veins appear patent.  There is no intrahepatic biliary ductal
dilatation or periportal edema.  The spleen is unremarkable.  The gallbladder
is surgically absent.  The pancreas is largely fatty replaced and is otherwise
normal in appearance.  There is minimal nodularity of the medial limb of the
right adrenal as noted previously.  The left adrenal is unremarkable.  The
kidneys demonstrate symmetric contrast enhancement and brisk bilateral
excretion without hydronephrosis or stones.

The patient is status post multiple abdominal surgeries with suture line seen
at the duodenum.  A PEG tube is in place with the pigtail seen within the
lumen of the stomach.  The stomach is distended with positive contrast and
appears normal.  The duodenum remains dilated, though this is not
significantly changed compared with prior.  There is no significant wall
thickening or differential enhancement of loops.  There is no intraperitoneal
free air or free fluid.

The aorta is normal in caliber along its course.  There is no pathologic
retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.

PELVIS:  The colon is normal in appearance along its course.  Oral contrast is
seen throughout the colon and into the rectum.  The bladder is normal in
appearance.  The uterus is unremarkable.

BONE WINDOWS:  There is no concerning lytic or blastic lesion.  Note is again
made of electrodes spanning the visualized T6-T8 levels.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Chronic-appearing duodenal dilation.  Contrast opacifies the entire GI
tract.
2.  PEG tube is stable in appearance.  There is no evidence for leak.
